final:
Fixed and verified.

## Bug
In `mergesort`, the base case only handled `len(arr) == 0`. For a single-element list `middle = 0`, so `right = mergesort(arr[0:])` — the same list — causing infinite recursion (and `left = []`). Any list of length 1 blew up.

## Fix
Changed the base case to `if len(arr) <= 1: return list(arr)` (returning a copy so the caller's input list isn't aliased into the output). The rest of the merge logic is unchanged; `left[i:] or right[j:]` is still safe because exactly one of the two slices is non-empty when the loop exits.

## Verification
- Public examples pass: `[-1,1,0] → [-1,0,1]`, `[1,1,1] → [1,1,1]`.
- Self-authored cases pass: empty list, single element, duplicates, negatives, already-sorted two-element list, and a length-8 mixed-sign case. Expected values follow the ascending-sort specification.

Limitations: I did not do an exhaustive property test or measure performance; correctness beyond these cases rests on the standard merge-sort argument.
